ruleSourceBodyKaj: Kongres Aksara Jawa I Yogyakarta 2021 — Tata Tulis Aksara Jawa (Simplified style), transliteration per JGST (Komisi I). User-facing Latin spelling follows PUJL (Balai Bahasa Yogyakarta). Predecessors: Wewaton Sriwedari 1926 and Pedoman Penulisan Aksara Jawa 2002. See docs/references/CITATIONS.md in the repository.
ruleSourceBodyPedoman: Pedoman Penulisan Aksara Jawa (Yayasan Pustaka Nusatama with the provincial governments of DIY, Central Java and East Java, 2002; the 1996 three-governor agreement). Where the Pedoman is silent, the app follows Kongres Aksara Jawa I Yogyakarta 2021 (Simplified style). Transliteration per JGST (Komisi I). User-facing Latin spelling follows PUJL (Balai Bahasa Yogyakarta). See docs/references/CITATIONS.md in the repository.

deviationTitle: How this differs from the traditional order
deviationBody: The traditional order ({ruleset}; see the About page) teaches the 20 nglegena letters row by row (ha na ca ra ka, da ta sa wa la, and so on) and introduces sandhangan only after all of them. This app differs in two ways. First, the nglegena letters are grouped by similar shape, the way Latin letters are taught in shape families (i l j, then r b p d). Letters that look alike are learned side by side, from simple shapes to complex ones. This grouping follows a teacher's suggestion and is still under review. Second, wulu (i) and suku (u) are pulled forward, straight after the first group pa ha ya. Without sandhangan every syllable sounds as a consonant + /a/, so a pupil can read very few words; with wulu and suku the vocabulary widens at once.
unitOrderBody:
1. Group 1: pa ha ya
2. wulu (i) and suku (u) — pulled forward
3. Group 2: ra ga la
4. Group 3: na ka ca sa
5. Group 4: da dha ja ta wa
6. Group 5: ba nga tha nya ma
7. remaining sandhangan
8. pasangan
9. advanced wing: murda and swara
Rekan, angka and pada are in the free-roam chart, ungated.
reviewHelpWhyBody: Memory fades fast. A short review just before you forget makes the letters stick — and every success stretches the gap: 10 minutes, then 1, 3, 8, 20 days.
reviewHelpRight: Right answer: the card comes back tomorrow, then less and less often.
reviewHelpWrong: Wrong answer: the card comes back right away, then again in 10 minutes.
reviewHelpStrength: Strength bars: new, okay, then strong. The longer you remember, the fuller they get.

engineErrorSlashPlacement: A “/” must come right after a final consonant.
engineErrorClusterWithoutConsonant: A cakra, pengkal or keret mark must follow a consonant.
engineErrorClusterClosesSyllable: A cakra, pengkal or keret mark cannot close a syllable.
engineErrorUnsupportedCluster: This consonant cluster is not supported.
engineErrorUnsupportedOnset: This cluster at the start of a syllable is not supported.
engineErrorPepetHiatus: Two vowels in a row after a pepet (ě) are not supported.
engineErrorVowelOnlySyllable: A syllable without a consonant needs a vowel.
engineErrorMurdaNotInRuleset: This murda is not part of Pedoman 2002 (only na, ka, ta, sa, pa, ga, ba).
engineErrorMurdaNotInitial: In Pedoman 2002, murda is written only on the first aksara of a word.
engineErrorSandhanganWithoutBase: A sandhangan has no base aksara.
engineErrorCecakTeluBase: Cecak telu is on an aksara that cannot take it.
engineErrorSecondVowelSign: One aksara has two vowel signs.
engineErrorUnrecognizedCodepoint: {codepoint} is not a recognized Javanese character.
engineAmbiguousBareE: A plain “e” can be pepet (ě) or taling (é). Pick one, or type ě/ê/é/è.
engineAmbiguousVowelPair: In Pedoman 2002, “ai”/“au” is two aksara: ha between the vowels (sinahu) or a swara letter. Pick one, or type the h.
engineAmbiguousBareEAndVowelPair: A plain “e” can be pepet (ě) or taling (é), and “ai”/“au” is two aksara (ha or a swara letter). Pick one.
traceFail: Not quite. Follow the lines again.
